title.narrative: Pillar 1: Provision of protection and health services to 720 Elderly Palestinian Refugees in Nahr El-Bared, Beddawi, and Wavel camps.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif font-size: 8pt text-align: justify"gtPalestinian refugees in Lebanon have been residing in unfavorable and inhumane conditions made worse by an unprecedented economic crisis and a political vacuum that have driven the country into new depths of despair and a series of internal struggles, especially in camps located in the North and Baalbeck. Amongst the most vulnerable groups suffering the repercussions of these conditions are the elderly refugees due to a combination of factors related to their age, displacement, exceptional needs, and limited access to essential resources, including protection and healthcare. Elderly people have been hit hard by the crisis in Lebanon. High rates of poverty and unemployment across the country made it very difficult for most to meet their basic needs, severely affecting their health and social status. According to the Population Census of Palestinian Refugees (2017), the elderly in Lebanon constitute 11% of the population, with a life expectancy of 78 years for men and 82 years for women. The Palestinian elderly aged 50 and above constitute 6.6% of the Palestinian refugees in Lebanon. Although this percentage is the highest among Arab countries, Lebanon is still one of the weakest countries in the region in securing social protection for the elderly. About 80% of the elderly in Lebanon depend on their families for financial support with most senior citizens receiving no pension or financial support from the state or any other agency.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size: 8pt text-align: justify font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtAccordingly, this project aims to provide a multisectoral approach to address the unique challenges faced by elderly refugees residing in three Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon, includinglt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt text-align: justify font-family:"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt text-align: justify font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtNahr el Bared camp (Akkar, Mhammara), Beddawi camp (Tripoli, Trablous El Qobbee) and Wavel Camp (Baalbeck). It focuses on providing essential health and protection services to promote their well-being and enhance their quality of life. By recognizing their specific needs and vulnerabilities, the project aims to create a supportive environment that respects their dignity and offers needed assistance. Thus, to ensure effectiveness, Taawon (Welfare Association) in partnership with four experienced sub-IPs (Women’s Program Association, Social Support Society, Mousawat, and Health Care Society) will improve the living conditions and reduce the protection risks of marginalized elderly Palestinian refugees, aged 65 and above. Together the consortium of partners will be providing access to medical homecare and follow up services, recreational activities, physiotherapy, assistive devices and hospitalization support to around 800 elderly persons with and without disability.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif font-size: 8pt text-align: justify"gtThe project will coordinate with a number of active stakeholders, including UNRWA and Palestine Red Crescent Society. It will also build on and complement the capacity building program of the Palestinian Disability Forum and other NGOs targeting disabled persons, as well as Taawon’s ongoing support for the elderly, such as its support to access kidney dialysis lifesaving services and mental health program. This project is in line with SDG2 “Zero Hunger”, SDG3 “Good Health and Well Being”, and SDG5 “Gender Equality”. All the services will be in line with WHO Guidelines on Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) and United Nations Principles for Older Persons.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt
